newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 12.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** An anticipated increase in government-set oil prices will keep Indian shares on a tight leash this week, but the market can take comfort from the safe passage last week of a business-friendly budget, brokers say
Analysts expect the government to raise prices of petroleum products to partially offset a 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) deficit in the oil-pool account, which is hurting oil refiners
** India needs to act quickly to ensure that large subsidies on oil are cut back and the government is considering a mix of options to tackle the issue, finance minister Palaniappan Chidambaram says

"The Prime Minister has started a debate by indicating that the question cannot be ducked for too long. Some arrangement has to be made, some decision has to be taken," Chidambaram told Reuters Financial Television in Japan where is attending the annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank
** The decision-making Steering Committee of India's ruling United Front coalition will meet on May 25 to discuss ways to contain the country's gaping oil pool deficit, the alliance's spokesman says

Jaipal Reddy told reporters the panel, which met on Saturday, could not take a decision on plugging the deficit because neither Finance Minister P. Chidambaram nor junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu were present
** Chidambaram says the rupee is currently at the right level and he sees no need for intervention

Asked to comment on the view of some analysts that the rupee was overvalued and should be weakened, Chidambaram told Reuters Financial Television in Japan "No, I do not think we should induce a depreciation just to boost someone's confidence. Once you say the rupee will find its level in the market, then you must leave it to the market"

** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has relaxed norms for borrowings by term lending institutions. The central bank has decided to fix an "umbrella limit" on total borrowings by the institutions instead of the current "instrument-wise" limit, it said in a statement

** Videocon International Ltd's $35 million floating rate note issue is now in general syndication, bankers say. The facility has a final maturity of three years, with no put or call options. It was priced at par to float at 185 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
** Indian shares end mixed on Friday with Bombay's benchmark stocks index closing 15.84 points, or 0.42 percent, higher at 3769.34
** The National exchange index drops 0.70 points to 1053.35, the Delhi index slips 5.42 points to 771.91 and the Madras index falls 0.62 to 3,641.87, but the Calcutta index gains 0.63 to 106.22
